test_title: PYST 18: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Under what circumstances can the Parliament legislate on a subject in the State List?

options.text: When Rajya Sabha passes a resolution

solution:
The correct answer is __**When Rajya Sabha passes a resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 249** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Parliament** can legislate on a subject in the **State List** if the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution.
 
• This resolution must be supported by **not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting**, declaring that it is necessary or expedient in the **national interest** for the Parliament to make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the **State List**. ***Hence, the correct answer is When Rajya Sabha passes a resolution.***
 
• A law made under **Article 249** remains in force for a period of **one year** at a time. However, the **Rajya Sabha** can renew the resolution for subsequent periods of **one year** indefinitely.
 
• This provision highlights the **quasi-federal** nature of the **Indian Constitution**, where the **Union** is given overriding powers over state subjects under specific circumstances.
 
• Such a law ceases to have effect after **six months** from the date on which the resolution expires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 250 (During National Emergency)**: 
 
 
• The **Parliament** acquires the power to legislate with respect to any matter in the **State List** while a **Proclamation of Emergency** (under **Article 352**) is in operation.
 
• Such laws become inoperative **six months** after the emergency has ceased to operate.
 
 
 
• **Article 252 (Request by States)**: 
 
 
• If the **legislatures of two or more states** pass a resolution requesting the **Parliament** to enact laws on a **State List** subject, the Parliament can make such a law for those specific states.
 
• Any other state can adopt such a law later by passing a resolution in its legislature.
 
 
 
• **Article 253 (International Agreements)**: 
 
 
• The **Parliament** can make laws on any subject (including the **State List**) for implementing **international treaties**, **agreements**, or **conventions** with other countries or international bodies.
 
 
 
• **Article 356 (President’s Rule)**: 
 
 
• When **President’s Rule** is imposed in a state, the **Parliament** is authorized to exercise the legislative powers of that **State Legislature**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** divides legislative powers into three lists: the **Union List (List I)**, the **State List (List II)**, and the **Concurrent List (List III)**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha**, acting as the **Council of States**, serves as the protector of the states' interests. Therefore, its consent is mandatory under **Article 249** to allow central interference in state subjects.
 
• During a **Financial Emergency** (under **Article 360**), the **Union** can give directions to states regarding **financial propriety** and the reservation of **Money Bills** for the **President's** consideration, but it does not automatically transfer the entire **State List** legislative power to **Parliament**.
 
• The **issuance of an ordinance** by the **President** (under **Article 123**) generally applies to matters on which the **Parliament** can legislate; hence, it cannot be used to legislate on **State List** subjects unless the aforementioned special circumstances (like Emergency or Rajya Sabha resolution) already exist.

5f
